title: Hybrid entitlement experiment: tiered observability retention + compliance pack + premium SLA
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Run a controlled pricing and entitlement experiment that tests a hybrid packaging model combining (A) tiered observability retention, (B) an enterprise compliance pack, and (C) an optional premium SLA add-on.

Background: Sales and CSMs have requested clearer packaging for enterprise observability needs (longer retention + token-level cost breakdown), while Legal and Security want an easier way to sell and validate a compliance bundle (audit logs, KMS integrations, enhanced questionnaire responses). Engineering prefers small incremental rollouts that avoid complex per-account billing changes.

Experiment hypothesis: Offering a self-serve "observability retention tiering" option plus a separate "compliance pack" (one-time entitlement with managed questionnaire and audit artifacts) and a paid premium-SLA add-on will increase deal size and conversion from self-serve to sales-assisted by 15% over baseline within 90 days, without materially increasing support tickets (>10% delta).

Scope: - Product UI for per-route retention selector (30/90/365 days) in Console + per-token cost preview. - New entitlement for "Compliance Pack" which toggles audit log retention, KMS/HSM integration guide, and expedited security questionnaire assistance. - Premium SLA product page that lists latency and uptime targets; behind a feature flag for canary tenants. - Billing experiment: two pricing cells to test: (1) retention tiers charged as fixed monthly addon, (2) retention tiers charged as per-GB usage; Compliance Pack as flat fee vs included in Dedicated.

Out-of-scope: Dedicated capacity procurement changes, deep changes to billing ledgers (we will implement via coupon/plan sandbox for experiment), major UI redesigns.

Success metrics: - +15% ARPA for accounts that opt into any addon during experiment window. - Net conversion lift from free trial to paid by +8% in canary group. - Support ticket delta <= 10% for onboarding flows. - Time-to-close (sales cycles) for enterprise contracts reduced by 7% when Compliance Pack is offered.

Key trade-offs: - Self-serve pricing keeps sales motion light but reduces immediate ARR capture; sales-assisted pricing may increase friction. - Fixed monthly pricing is simpler for customers but may over/undercharge depending on actual retention volumes. - Implementing entitlement gating in Console quickly could add temporary UX debt but speeds experiment rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Console exposes retention tier selector (30/90/365) on per-route settings for canary tenants and shows token-level cost estimate.
Compliance Pack entitlement can be toggled on tenant level via Console and creates an internal ticket for SecOps assistance (automated CC to compliance@redwood.com).
Premium SLA add-on page is published behind feature flag with clear SLOs; billing sandbox recognizes addon purchases for experiment tenants.
A/B experiment framework records opt-in, conversion, ARPA and support ticket counts for treatment vs control groups.
Security questionnaire template updated and a one-click export of audit artifacts implemented in Drive/Confluence links for customers who purchase Compliance Pack.
No critical incidents from rollout; any P0/P1 incidents captured and triaged within 24 hours.
Experiment telemetry dashboard created and validated (latency, opt-in rate, ARR delta, support tickets).

decisions: Decide-1: Run 2x pricing treatments in parallel (fixed monthly addon vs usage-based per-GB) to measure revenue + support impact.
Decide-2: Implement Compliance Pack as a purchasable entitlement separate from Dedicated; include expedited questionnaire assistance as part of the pack for the experiment.
Decide-3: Use feature flags to restrict premium SLA offering to canary tenants to limit exposure and enable fast rollback.
Decide-4: Use sandboxed billing metadata to simulate charges to avoid full ledger changes during the experiment window.
